name: OPK-88004

lead: OPK-88004 is an experimental SARM tested in testosterone-deficient prostate cancer survivors and in men with BPH. In the survivor trial it increased lean mass and lowered fat mass.
It did not improve sexual symptoms or physical performance, and the BPH trial was terminated.

paras: It is an oral non-steroidal androgen receptor modulator intended to act on muscle with less effect on the prostate.
The survivor trial reported no PSA recurrence or erythrocytosis. Oral SARMs have been reported to suppress HDL cholesterol. It is not approved for any use.

lead: OPK-88004, also known as LY-2452473, is an investigational non-steroidal selective androgen receptor modulator (SARM). It has been studied for androgen deficiency symptoms in prostate cancer survivors and for benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH).[1][2][3]

In a randomized trial of 114 testosterone-deficient men who had undergone prostatectomy for low-grade prostate cancer, it increased lean body mass and reduced fat mass, but did not improve sexual symptoms or physical performance, and no PSA recurrence was seen.[1] A phase 2 BPH trial was terminated.[3] It is not approved for any use.

paras: In the prostate cancer survivor trial, OPK-88004 produced a dose-related increase in whole-body lean mass and a decrease in fat mass, but sexual symptoms and physical performance did not improve.[1] A 2025 systematic review of randomized trials of SARMs covers the class more broadly.[4]

In the prostate cancer survivor trial, no participant had PSA recurrence or erythrocytosis.[1] A separate analysis of the same compound found that oral SARMs suppress HDL cholesterol and examined its effects on HDL particle function, cholesterol efflux capacity and particle size.[2]

A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial enrolled 114 men (average age 67.5) with symptomatic testosterone deficiency after radical prostatectomy for low-grade, organ-confined prostate cancer. The authors concluded OPK-88004 was safe with respect to PSA recurrence and increased lean mass but did not improve sexual symptoms or physical performance.[1] A follow-up analysis examined its effect on HDL function.[2] A phase 2 trial in men with signs and symptoms of BPH (NCT03297398, 114 participants, started 2018) was terminated.[3]

The sources reviewed do not document use of OPK-88004 in looksmaxxing communities; it appears in the literature as an investigational drug in clinical trials, and SARM detection methods used in anti-doping testing include its code name LY-2452473.

timeline.event: Phase 2 BPH trial begins and is later terminated.[3]
Prostate cancer survivor trial results published.[1]
